chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Everything that befalls the slave while he is in the state of Ihram, the expiation is upon the master, if he permitted him to enter into Ihram.

key_terms.أَصَابَ: Befalls or occurs (referring to ritual errors)
key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One who is in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for the expiation if a slave makes a mistake during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the vicarious liability of the master in the context of Hajj, establishing that if he grants permission for his slave to perform the pilgrimage, he assumes responsibility for any ritual defects or omissions committed by the slave. This ruling underscores the master's role as the primary agent in the slave's religious obligations when authorization is given, a principle deeply rooted in Shia fiqh regarding the legal capacity of slaves. It highlights the practical implication that the master cannot claim ignorance of the slave's ritual state if he initiated the permission, thereby ensuring the validity of the Hajj for the slave.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Everything which the slave commits while he is in Ihraam, so it (expiation) is upon the master when he permits to him to be in the Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whatever a slave may commit in the state of Ihram is on his master, if he gives him permission to assume the state of Ihram.’”
